Zamosc New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zamość, Poland

Demolished. This is the newer of Zamość's two Jewish cemeteries, a companion to the Old cemetery documented elsewhere in this collection, serving the same city that produced Rosa Luxemburg, I.L. Peretz, and Izrael Segal ben Mosze. It served as the city's main burial ground until WWII; in 1942, victims of the ghetto's liquidation were buried here in mass graves. Around 1969, Bohaterów Monte Cassino Street was paved directly through the cemetery, and part of the site was taken over by the 'Cora' clothing factory. As recently as 2017, city authorities paved another street, K. Namysłowskiego, through the cemetery, and graves were dug up during construction. The only surviving structure from the cemetery is its former funeral home, now refurbished into a residential building.
